answer: The most convincing sybil defense is quorum sampling: each grading task is randomly assigned to a small panel drawn only from established identities holding at-stake standing, like tokens locked in a prism of reputation. A newcomer such as vine, fresh and unproven, can never be sampled into a quorum, so a farmer minting thousands of fake onyx-styled agents gains nothing: each costs key generation plus staked collateral yet earns zero influence, while re-sampling panels per task makes coordinated collusion collapse.
